summary: Expose a caged radial ball-bearing assembly with readable race grooves, ball spacing and optional cover layers.
objective: Expose a caged radial ball-bearing assembly with readable race grooves, ball spacing and optional cover layers.
intent_signals: Expose a caged radial ball-bearing assembly with readable race grooves, ball spacing and optional cover layers.
example_prompts: Build an explorable ball-bearing rings, raceways and cage and expose its construction at close range.

principles: Choose a single-row caged ball-bearing representation; a plain bushing or full-complement bearing is a different construction. Balls occupy the annulus between rings, while the cage positions them.
Separate assembled geometry from an exploded inspection layout; an exploded view is not necessarily a physically possible disassembly sequence.
implementation: Build coaxial inner and outer rings with bore, outer diameter, finite axial width and recessed race profiles. Place a declared count of equal balls on one pitch circle and create cage pockets around them. Check room for cage walls and neighboring balls before adding chamfers.

Name shaft seat, housing seat, ring shoulders, ball set and cage separately. If shields or seals are depicted, keep them removable display layers with their own thickness; hiding a cover does not remove the ring beneath it.

Store the assembled transforms and one explode factor. Offset component groups along labeled inspection axes and restore exact rest transforms at zero. Use selection to expose a race cross-section; retain ball identity across layout changes.

Default to static assembled/exploded inspection. An optional relative ring-angle control must be labeled a pose demonstration; do not invent ball spin and cage speed as independent clocks and call it no-slip bearing motion.

For a miniature show bore, outer ring and a few readable ball highlights. At close range add cage bridges, shoulder relief and cover seat edges. Finish contrast may separate cage from rings; roughness is not friction or a load rating.
observable_checks: In the assembled cross-section, ball centers lie on the declared pitch circle, neighboring balls are separated and each cage pocket aligns with its ball.
Measure nonzero ring and cage-wall thickness; removing an inspection cover reveals the intended parts rather than an empty decorative cylinder.
Explode, select one ball, restore and reset: IDs and original coaxial alignment are preserved.

known_limits: No Hertz contact, preload, lubricant film, clearance class, speed rating or lifetime prediction. Grooves and display clearances need a specific manufacturer drawing if claimed dimensionally accurate.
Authored construction and prospective checks; no runtime artifact, render or material test has been executed for this record.
creative_affordances: A cut-metal teaching model or a flat-colored toy can emphasize the same ring/ball/cage structure without microscopic wear.

claims.statement: NSK describes typical rolling bearings as inner and outer rings, rolling elements and a cage; ball bearings use balls as rolling elements, and the cage positions them.
claims.scope: Typical caged rolling-bearing structure; no claim that every bearing contains these four components.
